title: One foundation for agents you use and agents you build.
lead: Build an agent into your TypeScript application with the SDK. Or work in your terminal with the coding CLI built from the same public components. Configure a model endpoint, tools, permissions, and sessions for the task at hand.
heroNote: Public packages · Node.js 22.12 or later · Bring a model endpoint
heroVision: Our direction: agents that can reliably advance the systems they are built on.
proofTitle: Inspect the pieces. Then run a first query.
proofLead: The agent framework assembles sessions, tools, and permission checks. The coding CLI is one maintained interface built on it. You can use the framework from your own Node.js application.
diagramCaption: One public TypeScript foundation, with an embeddable path and a ready terminal interface.

tasks.title: Build a query into your app
tasks.body: Install the framework and a provider adapter, then call createQuery from a Node.js script. Move to InteractiveSession when your own UI needs a longer conversation.
tasks.needs: You need Node.js 22.12+, a configured provider endpoint, and a model ID. The example on this page uses a running local OpenAI-compatible server.

tasks.title: Ask the coding CLI about a project
tasks.body: Run the CLI, configure a provider and model with a hosted key or running local endpoint, then decide whether to trust the workspace before project context is loaded.
tasks.needs: You need Node.js 22.12+ and an API key or a running local model server. Provider costs and policies depend on the endpoint you choose.

featuresLead: Every capability below is part of the public SDK packages or the coding CLI built from them. Each card names the package, class, flag, or command to look for and links to the guide that owns the details.

models.title: Models and providers
models.body: Choose the model per task, and keep a turn going when one fails.

safety.title: Tools and safety
safety.body: Typed tools, with every call checked before it runs.

sessions.title: Sessions and execution
sessions.body: Long-running work that survives the terminal and splits across agents.

extend.title: Connect and extend
extend.body: Bring in servers, skills, and plugins without forking the runtime.

interfaces.title: Interfaces
interfaces.body: The same session behind a terminal, a script, a browser, or a protocol.

build.title: Build your own
build.body: Use the layers directly, or assemble a product of your own on them.

providers.title: Multi-provider adapters
providers.body: Provider packages for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen and Gemma, plus any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (gateways, Azure, vLLM, local servers) through baseURL.

fallback.title: Fallback, effort and advisor
fallback.body: FallbackProvider moves a turn to another model when the primary is overloaded or failing. The CLI adds per-run model effort and an advisor model the agent can consult.

local.title: Local models
local.body: Point a provider profile at an Ollama, LM Studio or other OpenAI-compatible server on your own machine or network. You run the model; enabled tools decide what else leaves it.

media.title: Image and video generation
media.body: The Gemini provider includes image generation, and a separate ByteDance (ModelArk) provider generates video. The video provider is not a chat model for an agent.

tools.title: Validated tools
tools.body: createZodFunctionTool checks model arguments against a zod schema before your function runs. Built-in coding tools cover files, search, shell, web fetch and web search.

permissions.title: Permission modes and rules
permissions.body: Every tool call passes deny, ask and allow rules, then one of five permission modes. A few destructive actions are never approved automatically in any mode.

hooks.title: Lifecycle hooks
hooks.body: Run commands on tool, prompt and session events. PreToolUse can block a call; other hooks log, audit, or add context to the next prompt.

sandbox.title: OS sandbox for shell
sandbox.body: Shell commands can run inside bubblewrap on Linux and WSL2 or Seatbelt on macOS, limiting what a command can read, write, or reach on the network.

trust.title: Workspace trust
trust.body: Project instructions such as AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md load only in a trusted workspace. An untrusted repository refuses unattended runs or starts them Restricted.

sessions.title: Saved, resumable sessions
sessions.body: Continue, resume, rename or fork a conversation. Context is tracked and compacted automatically; the SDK host supplies the session store it wants.

daemon.title: Background sessions and daemon
daemon.body: Supervised sessions keep running after the terminal closes. One workspace daemon serves several terminals and the desktop app from a single runtime.

subagents.title: Subagents and background tasks
subagents.body: Delegate work to subagents with their own context and tools, in process or in child processes, and manage queued and running jobs from one place.

automation.title: Loops, schedules and plans
automation.body: Repeat a prompt on a cadence, wake the agent later or when command output matches, and keep a session read-only until you approve its plan.

checkpoints.title: Checkpoints, memory and cost
checkpoints.body: Rewind or fork from edit checkpoints, keep approved facts across sessions with opt-in memory, inspect context use, and set a monthly cost budget.

workflows.title: DAG workflows
workflows.body: /workflows designs a workflow from a description with the active model, saves it as JSON in the workspace, validates it and runs it, optionally detached.

roundtable.title: Multi-agent roundtables
roundtable.body: Coordinate independent agents and people in one shared transcript: select turns, run parallel groups, and plug a Robota session in as a participant or selector.

mcp.title: MCP in both directions
mcp.body: Connect to stdio or remote MCP servers, including OAuth sign-in, after explicit approval. Or serve a session as an MCP server over stdio or authenticated HTTP.

skills.title: Skills, commands and agents
skills.body: Markdown skills and commands become slash commands; agent definitions describe subagents. They are discovered in the project and your home directory.

plugins.title: Plugins and marketplaces
plugins.body: Install plugins that bundle skills, hooks, themes and MCP servers. SDK lifecycle plugins cover history, logging, usage, limits, errors, analytics and webhooks.

events.title: External events
events.body: Grant a verified outside service permission to send text events into a running terminal session, and list or revoke those grants from the session.

terminal.title: Terminal UI
terminal.body: An interactive terminal app with a command menu, prompt history search, rebindable keys, file attachments with @path, and a plain-text screen-reader mode.

print.title: Print mode and goals
print.body: Run one prompt from a script or pipe, get text, JSON or streaming JSON, request schema-shaped output, or work toward a goal over several turns.

gui.title: Browser GUI and desktop app
gui.body: Serve the GUI for the current workspace on loopback and open it in a browser. The desktop app in the repository shows the same GUI over the workspace daemon.

http.title: Serve over HTTP and transports
http.body: Let other services submit turns and stream results as server-sent events, behind a bearer token or as an OAuth resource server. WebSocket, HTTP, MCP and WebRTC carriers share one wire protocol.

devices.title: Devices and remote control
devices.body: Message other live sessions, hand a conversation to another session or device, link your own devices, and co-drive a session from a paired browser over peer-to-peer WebRTC.

ci.title: CI and GitHub Actions
ci.body: Run print mode in a workflow step to review a pull request or answer a task, and gate a pipeline on an evals-as-code score.

core.title: Conversation engine
core.body: ConversationAgent runs and streams turns with history, tool calling, structured output and plugins. It is the minimal set: core plus one provider.

framework.title: Framework assembly
framework.body: createQuery runs one-shot queries with built-in tools and permissions; InteractiveSession drives a full conversation; createAgentRuntime assembles a host runtime.

embedding.title: Servers, bots and serverless
embedding.body: Put the framework behind an SSE or WebSocket server with a full event stream per session, resume a saved session per bot channel, or run a stateless runtime that persists nothing.

channels.title: One agent, many channels
channels.body: TransportRegistry runs one agent definition behind several transports, with their enabled state kept in a settings file; there is no separate gateway process.

product.title: Product composition
product.body: assembleProduct builds a product from a declarative profile. Capability packs, slash-command modules, presets and output styles are the parts the coding CLI uses.

productHost.title: Ship your own CLI product
productHost.body: Depend on the published CLI package and own the entry, identity, assets and packaging: a product-bound CLI host, desktop-host helpers for an Electron app, and native binary builds.

analytics.title: Diagnostics, usage and evals
analytics.body: Check settings, provider, trust and plugins in one report; summarize local token use and cost without sending content; export content-free metrics; run evals as code.

cliTitle: A full agent in your terminal.
cliLead: The CLI is the maintained interface on the shared foundation. The same runtime powers the terminal UI, scripts, background sessions, the browser GUI, and other services.

cliFlows.title: Work interactively
cliFlows.body: Start a session, choose a permission mode, or switch to a screen-reader mode.

cliFlows.title: Script a single prompt
cliFlows.body: Print mode exits with a code your script can check. A goal run keeps working over several turns.

cliFlows.title: Keep sessions running
cliFlows.body: Resume earlier work, run supervised sessions in the background, and share one daemon.

cliFlows.title: Serve it to other surfaces
cliFlows.body: Open the browser GUI, accept HTTP clients with a bearer token, or act as an MCP server.

cliFlows.title: Reach your other sessions
cliFlows.body: Inside a session: message peers, hand off a conversation, link devices, pair a browser.

cliFlows.title: Check setup and usage
cliFlows.body: Diagnose configuration, summarize local usage, check for updates, and run evals.

safetyTitle: Decide what the agent may do.
safetyLead: Deny, ask and allow rules are checked first, then the permission mode. Set the mode per run or change it inside a session.

safetyNotes.title: Rules win over modes
safetyNotes.body: An ask rule still asks in bypassPermissions. Removing the root, home or working directory, and writing into .git or tool configuration, are never approved automatically.

safetyNotes.title: Unattended means denied
safetyNotes.body: In default mode, a request that needs approval is denied when nobody answers it, unless your host supplies a permission handler.

safetyNotes.title: Sandboxed shell
safetyNotes.body: Combine permission rules with the OS sandbox so an approved command still runs with limited file and network access.

safetyLink: Read the permissions and hooks guide
architectureLead: Everything under packages/ is neutral and reusable; the CLI and apps are opinionated assemblies of those libraries. Each layer builds only on the layers below it.

layers.interface: Product interface: the terminal coding assistant
layers.composition: Product composition: profiles, capability packs, commands, presets
layers.surfaces: Terminal UI and carriers over the shared wire protocol
layers.runtime: Runtime: sessions, background tasks, tools, MCP client, plugins
layers.foundation: Foundation: the conversation engine and its contracts

packagesLead: Every package is published on npm under @robota-sdk/ and shares one version. Start with the smallest set your task needs.

start.title: Start here
start.body: The engine, one provider per vendor, and validated tools.

assembly.title: App assembly
assembly.body: Sessions, permissions, background work, MCP, plugins and analysis.

multiAgent.title: Multi-agent conversation
multiAgent.body: Shared transcripts for independent agents and people.

composition.title: Product composition
composition.body: Build your own product on the same runtime.

transports.title: Transports and UI
transports.body: Put a session behind a protocol or a screen.

cli.title: Agent interface
cli.body: The coding CLI, published as a self-contained bundle.

installTitle: Pick how you want to run it.
installLead: Published packages need Node.js 22.12 or later. The standalone binary needs nothing else installed.

npx.title: Run without installing
npx.body: Fetch and start the latest CLI with npx.

global.title: Install globally
global.body: Keep the CLI on your PATH with npm.

binary.title: Standalone binary
binary.body: The installer picks the binary for your OS and CPU from the latest release and verifies its SHA-256 checksum. Binaries are unsigned, so macOS and Windows may warn.

sdk.title: Embed the minimal SDK
sdk.body: The engine plus one provider package. Add agent-tools when the agent calls tools.

fitTitle: Use the source. Understand the terms.
fitLead: A public codebase lets you inspect how the SDK and CLI are assembled. Start with the package and source that match your task.

fitItems.title: Open source and commercial paths
fitItems.body: The code is offered under AGPL-3.0, with a commercial licensing path for uses that need different terms. Review the license for your distribution or service.

fitItems.title: Provider costs are separate
fitItems.body: The SDK and CLI do not include model inference. A hosted provider can charge for usage; local inference has its own compute and operating costs.

fitItems.title: First-party showcase
fitItems.body: The coding CLI is the maintained example of these public components composed into a developer tool. Browse its source and the current showcase.

visionTitle: Our agents develop and advance our agents.
visionBody: That is the long-term direction of the project. Today, the usable foundation is an SDK and coding CLI with explicit providers, tools, and host decisions. Reliable autonomous self-development must be demonstrated through actual outcomes as the system evolves.
roadmapNote: Roadmap reviewed October 2026. Plans can change; the public beta is available now.

faqs.question: Do I need the CLI to use the SDK?
faqs.answer: No. Import the agent framework into your own Node.js host and inject a provider. The CLI is one complete interface built from public components.

faqs.question: Will a query run without configuring a model?
faqs.answer: You need a provider endpoint and a suitable model. A local OpenAI-compatible example requires its server and model to be running; a hosted provider needs its own credentials and terms.

faqs.question: Does the SDK persist conversations automatically?
faqs.answer: No. A simple createQuery call is not a durable session. Supply a session store when your host needs save and resume behavior.

faqs.question: What should I read before enabling tools?
faqs.answer: Review project trust and permission modes. In default mode, an unattended request for approval is denied unless your host provides a permission handler.

faqs.question: Is the beta API stable?
faqs.answer: Not yet. The packages are 3.0.0 beta releases and APIs may change before a stable release; the changelog records upgrade notes.

closeBody: Choose the embeddable query or set up the coding CLI. Both paths begin with the provider and access decisions you control.
